deep.name: Felis catus
deep.source: Domestic cats; published estimates vary widely

deep.name: Gorilla beringei
deep.source: IUCN Red List: mountain (~1,060) + Grauer's (~3,800) gorillas

deep.name: Ailuropoda melanoleuca
deep.source: China's Fourth National Giant Panda Survey (2015)

deep.name: Loxodonta africana
deep.source: African Elephant Status Report 2016 (~415k African elephants of both species)

deep.name: Passer domesticus
deep.source: Callaghan et al. 2021, PNAS (house sparrow, the most numerous wild bird)

deep.name: Quelea quelea
deep.source: Red-billed quelea, often cited as the most numerous wild bird

deep.name: Euphausia superba
deep.source: Antarctic krill biomass ~380 Mt (Atkinson et al. 2009) / ~1 g per krill

deep.name: Apis mellifera
deep.source: ~100 million managed hives (FAOSTAT 2022) x 20-50 thousand bees, plus wild colonies

anchors.name: Bacteria
anchors.source: Flemming & Wuertz 2019, Nat Rev Microbiol (1.2e30 prokaryotes); Whitman et al. 1998, PNAS (4-6e30)

anchors.name: Archaea
anchors.source: ~10% of prokaryote biomass (Bar-On et al. 2018) applied to the prokaryote total

anchors.name: Cyanobacteria
anchors.source: Flombaum et al. 2013, PNAS: Prochlorococcus 2.9e27 + Synechococcus 7e26 (ocean only)

anchors.name: Fungi
anchors.source: Cell-equivalents: 12 Gt C of fungal biomass (Bar-On et al. 2018) / ~5e-12 g C per yeast-sized cell; fungi have no countable individual

anchors.name: SAR
anchors.source: Typical protist densities (soil ~1e4-1e5 per g, surface ocean ~1e3 per mL) over global soil and ocean volumes

anchors.name: Embryophyta
anchors.source: Shoots and ramets; grassland shoot densities (~1e3-1e4 per m2) over ~5e13 m2. Trees alone: 3.04e12 (Crowther et al. 2015, Nature)

anchors.name: Nematoda
anchors.source: van den Hoogen et al. 2019, Nature (soil only, so a lower bound)

anchors.name: Copepoda
anchors.source: Widely cited figure; primary source unclear

anchors.name: Insecta
anchors.source: Williams 1964 via the Smithsonian ('10 quintillion insects alive at any time')

anchors.name: Collembola

anchors.name: Formicidae
anchors.source: Schultheiss et al. 2022, PNAS (conservative)

anchors.name: Aves
